config.title: Location & Store Finder

intro.title: Location & Store Finder
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a mobile app that helps users find nearby stores using their device's location. You'll learn how to access the device's GPS capabilities through Capacitor's Geolocation API to get the user's current position. The core programming concept involves working with asynchronous operations and promises to handle location data retrieval. You'll use Ionic components to display a map and store locations, along with Angular services to manage the location logic. By the end, you'll have a functional store finder that can display nearby locations based on real GPS coordinates.
intro.usecase: Location-aware store finders are essential features in retail, food delivery, and service apps like Starbucks, Domino's, or Home Depot. Users need to find nearby physical locations, check operating hours, and get directions—all requiring precise geolocation integration. As a developer, you'll implement this pattern using Ionic's UI components for maps and lists, Capacitor for native device location access, and Angular services to manage state and API calls. This teaches you how to bridge web technologies with native device capabilities to create practical, user-focused mobile experiences.

objectives: Implement Ionic components to construct the user interface for a store finder application.
Apply Angular services to encapsulate location-related business logic separate from components.
Utilize the Capacitor Geolocation plugin to access the device's current GPS coordinates.
Execute conditional logic to handle permission states when requesting location access.
Define and invoke methods to retrieve nearby store data based on user coordinates.
Construct observable data streams to manage asynchronous location and store data.
Implement Angular template syntax to display store information dynamically in the UI.
Apply Ionic's ion-list and ion-item components to iterate through and display store results.
Utilize mapping services (like Google Maps or OpenStreetMap) to display store locations visually.
Handle user interactions to select a store and display detailed information in a modal or page.
Store user preferences for location permissions and default search radius using Ionic Storage.
Implement error handling to manage cases when location services are unavailable or denied.

steps.hint: Use a single import statement with curly braces to import multiple components from the same package.
steps.analogousExample:

import { IonHeader, IonToolbar, IonTitle } from '@ionic/angular/standalone';

steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing Geolocation from the correct package '@capacitor/geolocation'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import Geolocation from '@capacitor/geolocation'.

steps.title: Create the StoreFinderComponent
steps.instruction: Create the main component class named StoreFinderComponent with the @Component decorator. Set the selector to 'app-store-finder' and the template to an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from Angular core to define your component. The selector should match what you'll use in HTML, and the template can be empty for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TypeScript class named StoreFinderComponent is created with the @Component decorator configured with selector 'app-store-finder' and an empty template.
successCriteria: The code should include: 1) A class named StoreFinderComponent, 2) The @Component decorator, 3) Selector set to 'app-store-finder', 4) Template set to an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the StoreFinderComponent class with the @Component decorator. This sets up the foundation for your location and store finder component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but something is missing. Make sure you have: 1) The class named StoreFinderComponent, 2) The @Component decorator, 3) Selector set to 'app-store-finder', 4) Template set to an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. You need to create a class named StoreFinderComponent with the @Component decorator, selector 'app-store-finder', and an empty template.

steps.title: Define component properties interface
steps.instruction: Inside the StoreFinderComponent class file, define a TypeScript interface named 'Store' with the following properties: id (number), name (string), address (string), distance (number), and isOpen (boolean).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TypeScript interface named Store is defined with the specified properties and types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Store interface with all required properties and proper TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the interface is missing some required properties or has incorrect type annotations. Check that all properties (id, name, address, distance, isOpen) are included with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Store interface wasn't defined correctly. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword, name it 'Store', and include all five properties with the specified TypeScript types.

steps.title: Initialize component state properties
steps.instruction: Inside the StoreFinderComponent class, declare the following properties with their initial values: stores (an empty array of Store objects), userLocation (an object with lat and lng properties initialized as null), isLoading (boolean initialized as false), and errorMessage (string initialized as empty).
steps.hint: Add these properties directly in the class body after the constructor (if any). Use TypeScript type annotations for each property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The StoreFinderComponent class now has four typed properties with their initial values: stores (empty array), userLocation (object with null lat/lng), isLoading (false), and errorMessage (empty string).
successCriteria: The component class contains the four properties with correct TypeScript types and initial values as specified.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully declared all the component properties with their initial values. This gives us a clean starting state for our location and store finder functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've declared some of the properties, but not all four. Make sure to include stores, userLocation, isLoading, and errorMessage with their correct types and initial values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component properties aren't declared correctly. You need to add four properties inside the StoreFinderComponent class with the specified types and initial values.

steps.title: Create getCurrentLocation method
steps.instruction: Inside the StoreFinderComponent class, create an async method named getCurrentLocation that will fetch the device's current position using the Geolocation plugin.
steps.hint: Define the method with the async keyword and use Geolocation.getCurrentPosition() to get the coordinates.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has an async method stub for getting the device's location.
successCriteria: The method should be named getCurrentLocation, marked as async, return a Promise<void>, and be defined inside the StoreFinderComponent class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the async method stub. Next, we'll implement the Geolocation call inside it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the method is named getCurrentLocation, uses the async keyword, and returns Promise<void>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method definition is missing or incorrect. Create an async method named getCurrentLocation that returns Promise<void> inside the component class.

steps.title: Create findNearbyStores method
steps.instruction: Inside the StoreFinderComponent class, create a new method called findNearbyStores that returns a Promise<void>.
steps.hint: Add a new method after getCurrentLocation. Use the async keyword and specify the return type as Promise<void>.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a new method named findNearbyStores that returns a Promise<void>.
successCriteria: The method must be named findNearbyStores, be async, and return Promise<void>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the findNearbyStores method. This method will be used to simulate fetching nearby stores in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the method is named findNearbyStores, uses the async keyword, and has the return type Promise<void>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method wasn't created correctly. Please create a method named findNearbyStores that is async and returns Promise<void>.

steps.title: Add basic template structure
steps.instruction: Update the component template to include a basic container structure inside the IonContent. Add a div with class 'ion-padding' and inside it add a paragraph element with the text 'Your location will appear here.'
steps.hint: Look for the comment '<!-- Content will go here -->' inside the IonContent. Replace it with a div containing a paragraph.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding basic structure inside IonContent

Your location will appear here.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now has a basic content structure with a padded container and placeholder text.
successCriteria: The IonContent should contain a div with class 'ion-padding' and inside it a paragraph element with the text 'Your location will appear here.'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the basic template structure with a container and placeholder text.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the div with class 'ion-padding' and the paragraph element with the exact text 'Your location will appear here.' inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure doesn't match what was requested. Look for the comment inside IonContent and replace it with a div containing a paragraph as shown in the example.

steps.title: Add location button and display
steps.instruction: Add an IonButton inside the ion-content that calls getCurrentLocation when clicked, and display the userLocation coordinates and errorMessage if they exist.
steps.hint: Use (click) to call getCurrentLocation, and use *ngIf to conditionally show the location and error messages.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes a button to trigger location fetching and displays location coordinates or error messages when available.
successCriteria: The learner must add an IonButton with (click) event binding to getCurrentLocation, and add conditional paragraphs to display userLocation coordinates and errorMessage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the location button and display logic. The button will trigger the location fetch, and the UI will show coordinates or errors when available.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some of the required elements. Make sure you have: 1) An IonButton with (click)="getCurrentLocation()", 2) A paragraph that shows userLocation coordinates using *ngIf, and 3) A paragraph that shows errorMessage using *ngIf.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't include the required elements. You need to add an IonButton that calls getCurrentLocation when clicked, and display paragraphs for userLocation coordinates and errorMessage using *ngIf.

steps.title: Add store finder button and loading state
steps.instruction: Add an IonButton to the template that triggers the findNearbyStores method when clicked, and conditionally show an IonSpinner when isLoading is true.
steps.hint: You'll need to add IonButton and IonSpinner to the imports, then add the button with a click handler and use *ngIf to conditionally show the spinner based on the isLoading property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will have a button to find stores and a loading spinner that appears when isLoading is true.
successCriteria: The learner must add IonButton and IonSpinner imports, add a button with (click) event bound to findNearbyStores, and conditionally show the spinner using *ngIf="isLoading".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the store finder button and loading spinner. The button will trigger the store search and the spinner provides visual feedback during loading.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but check that you've: 1) Added both IonButton and IonSpinner imports, 2) Created a button with (click)="findNearbyStores()", and 3) Used *ngIf="isLoading" to conditionally show the spinner.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the required store finder button and loading spinner. Remember to import the Ionic components, add the button with click handler, and conditionally display the spinner based on isLoading.

steps.title: Display store list
steps.instruction: Add an IonList component inside the ion-content to display the stores array using *ngFor, showing each store's name, address, distance, and open status.
steps.hint: Use the IonList and IonItem components from @ionic/angular/standalone to create a list. You'll need to import them first.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of displaying an array with *ngFor
<ion-list>
  <ion-item *ngFor="let item of items">
    <ion-label>{{ item.name }} - {{ item.description }}</ion-label>
  </ion-item>
</ion-list>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a list of stores with their details when the template renders.
successCriteria: The template includes an IonList with an IonItem for each store in the stores array, using *ngFor to iterate. Each item displays the store's name, address, distance, and open status.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the store list display using Ionic list components. The *ngFor directive iterates over the stores array and renders each store's details.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some of the required elements. Make sure you have an IonList with IonItem inside, using *ngFor="let store of stores" to iterate, and display all four store properties (name, address, distance, isOpen).
steps.feedbackWrong: The store list isn't displayed correctly. Check that you have an IonList with IonItem elements, use *ngFor to loop through the stores array, and show each store's name, address, distance, and open status.
